name: Saging: starchy bananas
description: Bananas (saging), especially starchy cooking varieties, were an old food plant of the islands, eaten boiled or roasted. Banana stands are easily flattened by typhoons.
sources: William Henry Scott, Barangay: Sixteenth-Century Philippine Culture and Society (Ateneo de Manila University Press, 1994)
Francisco Ignacio Alcina, Historia de las islas e indios de Bisayas (1668), trans. Cantius Kobak and Lucio Gutiérrez (UST Publishing House, 2002–2005)

lore.en: Bananas are among the oldest food plants of island Southeast Asia. Starchy kinds were boiled or roasted like root crops, and the leaves wrapped food for cooking. A banana stand grows quickly but its soft trunks are the first thing a strong typhoon flattens.
lore.fil: Ang saging ay kabilang sa pinakamatatandang halamang pagkain sa Timog-silangang Asya. Nilalaga o iniihaw ang malalambot na uri gaya ng lamang-ugat, at ibinabalot sa dahon ang pagkaing niluluto. Mabilis tumubo ang sagingan pero ang malalambot nitong puno ang unang pinababagsak ng malakas na bagyo.

inGame.en: A Sagingan gives fresh food that spoils if it isn't eaten or preserved, and typhoons often flatten it.
inGame.fil: Nagbibigay ang Sagingan ng sariwang pagkain na nasisira kung hindi kakainin o ipreserba, at madalas itong pabagsakin ng bagyo.
